title: A counter with a history of attempts
description: The time since the last event, the previous periods and personal notes. A new entry starts the count while keeping the history that came before.

blocks.text: A counter shows the time since the last check-in, but resetting it can hide the whole journey up to that point. One review author specifically values having the number of attempts kept. A log like that lets you go back to past records even when the current count has started over.

quote.text: I had been trying to quit my habit for a very long time. It wasn’t until I downloaded the Days Since app that allowed me to track my progress. It even kept up with how many times I reset the counter so I could tell myself to quit playing and just do it.

blocks.text: Keep the completed periods and the time of the new attempt. Let a wrong date be corrected and a note added if wanted. The current counter and the history should be visible separately, so that a new start doesn’t look like the deletion of the past.

Go through a person’s own way of keeping track with them. Do they need the periods, the notes, or only an exact date? Don’t credit the counter with the ability to deal with addiction: what is being tested here is how convenient a personal record is, not the outcome of treatment.
